author: eBible.org
title: World English Bible, Protestant 66-book edition (engwebp)
location: Matthew 5; Mark 7; Galatians 2–5; Romans 3, 7, 8, 10, 13; Acts 15; Luke 6, 12, 16, 18, 19; Mark 10, 12, 14; Matthew 6, 19, 25; 1 Corinthians 16; 2 Corinthians 8–9; Romans 12, 15; Acts 4; 1 Timothy 6
note: Chapter links in passage records point to this edition. Biblical text is linked, not republished in this repository.

author: Matthew V. Novenson
title: Law in the New Testament
location: Sections 2 ('Christ the end of the law') and 5 ('I have not come to abolish the law')
note: Discusses diversity within Paul and Matthew, including the possibility and limits of interpreting Matthew as a response to Pauline ideas.

author: Bradley M. Trout
title: The nature of the law's fulfilment in Matthew 5:17: An exegetical and theological study
location: Abstract; discussion of fulfilment and kingdom; Conclusion
note: Proposes a salvation-historical/kingdom interpretation of Matthew's fulfilment language. Interpretive proposal, not consensus.

author: Logan Williams
title: The Stomach Purifies All Foods: Jesus' Anatomical Argument in Mark 7.18–19
location: Abstract; sections on Mark 7.18–19 and alternative parsing
note: Argues against the conventional narrator-gloss reading of Mark 7:19c. One recent scholarly case, not a settled correction of all translations.

author: Matthew Thiessen
title: Paul and the Gentile Problem
location: Publisher abstract only (full monograph not checked)
note: Represents a Gentile-focused reading of Paul's legal arguments. Do not cite unseen chapters or pages.

author: American Bible Society
title: The Council in Jerusalem
note: Accessible comparative overview; distinguish Acts as narrative from Paul's first-person letter.

author: John M. G. Barclay
title: Rich Poverty: 2 Corinthians 8.1–15 and the Social Meaning of Poverty and Wealth
location: Full article: Introduction; Macedonians' Wealth-in-Poverty; Corinthians and Christ; Conclusions, especially discussion of 2 Cor 8:1–15
note: Full open-access article inspected. Interprets wealth in 2 Corinthians 8 in terms of giving and social relations, and explicitly cautions against pressure on poor donors.

author: L. L. Welborn
title: ‘That There May Be Equality’: The Contexts and Consequences of a Pauline Ideal
location: Publisher abstract only; full article behind access restriction
note: The abstract describes an ideal of economic equality in collection practices. No claims are made about detailed arguments on inaccessible pages.

author: Louis Ndekha
title: Praising the poor and blaming the rich: A panegyric reading of Luke 6:20–49 in Malawian context
location: Full online article; Abstract, discussion of Lukan blessings and woes, and context-specific application
note: A contextual reading using Greco-Roman praise and blame conventions; its Malawian application is one interpretive perspective, not universal scholarly consensus.

author: H. C. van Zyl
title: Discernment as 'not knowing' and 'knowing': a perspective from Matthew 25:31–46
location: Full online article, especially §2 (identity of 'least'), §3 (not knowing), and discussion of universal and particularist readings
note: Reviews both particularist and universal interpretations of 'the least of these', proposing an integrated reading.

author: Elizabeth Shively
title: Commentary on Mark 10:17–31
location: Full online commentary: context, rich man, and radical discipleship
note: A pastoral/lectionary commentary, not represented as a peer-reviewed journal article. Describes the particular man and broader call to self-denial.

author: Adam Kubiś
title: The Poor Widow's Mites: A Contextual Reading of Mark 12:41–44
location: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record only; full PDF not independently checked
note: The abstract argues for the widow as a positive example and acknowledges a competing negative/exploitation reading. Do not attribute unseen argumentation or page-specific claims.
